title: QuiX Quantum and Dutch Photonics Consortium Form National Mission for 100+ Qubit Computer - Quantum Computing Report
gist: QuiX Quantum leads a three-year Dutch PhotonDelta National Growth Fund mission (through Dec 2028) coordinating eight partners against a shared error budget to build the manufacturing and architecture base for a 100+ qubit universal photonic quantum processor.

insights.claim: QuiX Quantum leads a three-year mission under Phase II of the PhotonDelta National Growth Fund Integrated Photonics Programme, running through December 2028, to build the manufacturing and architectural foundations for a 100+ qubit universal photonic quantum processor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: State-backed industrial programme positions QuiX as the Netherlands' photonic quantum champion.
insights.locator: European photonic quantum developer QuiX Quantum

insights.claim: The Dutch mission coordinates eight academic and industrial partners across twelve system deliverables, optimizing sub-assemblies against a common error budget rather than funding isolated component research.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Error-budget-driven co-design is a sensible model for photonic scaling and a template for other national programs.
insights.quote: Rather than funding isolated component research, the Dutch mission coordinates developers to optimize sub-assemblies against a common error budget necessary for fault-tolerant scaling.

insights.claim: Measurement-based photonic architectures face compounding bottlenecks: optical losses in passive routing, non-deterministic photon emission, detector efficiency limits, and electronic latency in active feed-forward switching.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defines the component KPIs investors should track in photonic quantum.

insights.claim: Within the Dutch mission, Bruco-IC is developing flip-chip control ASICs targeting active feed-forward latencies below 10 ns, down from current 150 ns baselines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 15x latency cut is needed so feed-forward reconfigures switches before photons reach the next stage.

insights.claim: PHIX and MicroAlign target 0.1 dB per facet fibre-to-chip coupling loss via automated alignment and packaging, while imec supplies ultra-low-loss silicon nitride PICs and high-speed electro-optic modulators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Packaging loss at the chip boundary is a key hurdle; these suppliers are picks-and-shovels for photonic quantum.

insights.claim: University of Twente and Eindhoven University of Technology handle quasi-deterministic single-photon emitters, while Leiden University and TU/e develop waveguide-integrated photon-number-resolving detectors and SPAD arrays.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Dutch academic base covers source and detection layers of the stack.

insights.claim: Under the Netherlands–Taiwan TechBridge framework, QuiX Quantum partnered with Brillink on high-efficiency SPAD arrays and MicroAlign teamed with Largan on mass-producible ultra-low-loss fiber-array connections.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Taiwan's optics manufacturing base (e.g. Largan) is entering the photonic quantum supply chain.

insights.claim: QuiX Quantum's loss-tolerant Dedalo architecture targets logical-qubit demonstrations between 2028 and 2030, building on its delivery of universal hardware to the German Aerospace Center (DLR QCI).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sets a dated milestone to hold QuiX accountable against.
